A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical simulations, including convergence statistics over 10,000 initialisations, perturbation experiments, and string-method connectivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original convergence statistics, numerical validation of fixed-point predictions, stability experiments, and appendix analyses of finite dimensionality and constrained dynamics.

M1.justification: The teacher–student architecture, population loss, overlap ODEs, block-symmetric ansatz, and learning procedures are retained. The string method disappears as a supplementary landscape probe; the formula corrections do not establish a different implemented learning algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions study the same synthetic Gaussian teacher–student tasks, including well-specified and overparameterised networks. Finite-dimensional checks at d = 196, 392, and 784 and the Leaky ReLU and erf experiments remain; removing connectivity analyses does not change the represented data or prediction task.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same GD, 2L-GD, nGD, and onGD comparison. The corresponding appendix comparisons also remain. Removed string-method citations are not removed experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The entire connectivity-testing protocol is removed, including permuted endpoints, string evolution, and metric-based spline reparameterisation in v1 Appendix D. Separately, the retained stability appendix changes relaxation from 100,000 to 10,000 steps at learning rate 0.01. Both figure captions still specify 1,000 steps, leaving the actual budget and whether experiments were rerun unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 removes the substantial string-method investigation of barriers and flat connections: v1 Figure 3a, Figure 4, and Appendix F's neuron-exchange case studies. Perturbative stability, finite-dimensional robustness, activation comparisons, and constrained-dynamics analyses remain.

E5.justification: The retained experiments preserve their repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices, including 10,000-initialisation statistics and 20 independent stability perturbations with mean and standard-deviation reporting. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-reporting practices appear.

E6.justification: The barrier-versus-flat-path results and family-dependent connectivity findings in v1 Figures 3a, 4, and 13–14 are removed. Retained Tables 1–5 preserve their numerical values; for example, Table 1's global-minimum frequencies remain 13.09%, 59.29%, and 99.63%. The revision does not report improved convergence performance.

T1.justification: The core ODE, fixed-point, and SGD derivations remain. The auxiliary induced-distance definition and derivation in v1 Appendix D.1 are deleted. v2 also corrects factors in the population-gradient and overlap derivations, reconciles the main-text onGD constraint with WWᵀ = dI, and adds absolute values to overlap bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion withdraw the central claim that overparameterisation merges isolated minima into continuous flat manifolds through a topological transition. They instead foreground fixed-point families, destabilisation of low-order traps, persistence of higher-order traps, and increased empirical reachability of global minima.

C2.justification: The explanation of optimisation benefits shifts from disappearing barriers and connected manifolds to perturbative instability and changes in which fixed-point families attract trajectories. The stability appendix now describes escape toward lower-loss configurations rather than a global-minimum manifold. A sharper global geometric description becomes future work, and the direction-dependent connectivity discussion is removed.

D1.justification: New Appendix H discloses CPU hardware, memory, core allocations, Slurm parallelisation, job limits, and approximate stability-analysis runtime. A new Software and Data statement promises source-code release upon publication but supplies no access link. Implementation details for the removed string analysis disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds Garipov et al. (2018) and removes Weinan et al. (2002), Ren et al. (2007), Samanta and Weinan (2013), and Baldassi et al. (2020). Related-work positioning shifts from confirming connected manifolds to characterising fixed-point stability and reachability, while the broader literature coverage remains.

P1.justification: Focused rewrites update the abstract, contributions, related work, Section 3.1, and conclusion. v2 removes redundant wording in Result 2, updates the appendix outline, and adds Accessibility, Software and Data, Impact Statement, and computational-details sections. The main section sequence and most technical exposition remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 1 loses its overparameterised connectivity schematic, Figure 2 changes from horizontal to vertically stacked panels, and Figure 3 retains only the perturbation panel. Several connectivity figures disappear, while retained figures and tables are resized, reformatted, and relocated.

improvement.justification: v1's broad flat-connectivity claims were difficult to reconcile with Appendix F and Figure 14's barrier-bearing path. v2 improves alignment between claims and evidence by withdrawing that generalisation and leaving global geometry open. Formula corrections and computational disclosures also improve precision and reproducibility information. Removing the connectivity analyses reduces geometric detail, and conflicting stability budgets remain, so the net improvement is limited.
